title: The fppf quotient of a smooth algebraic-space groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $U$ be an $S$-scheme and $R$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$, an identity $e:U\to R$, inversion $j:R\to R$ and composition $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ give a groupoid: for each test scheme $T$, objects are $U(T)$, arrows are $R(T)$ with source $s$ and target $t$, and these operations obey the category and inverse laws, naturally in $T$. Assume $s$ and $t$ are smooth, with smoothness tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\mathcal P$ be this presheaf of groupoids and let $\mathcal Q=a_{fppf}\mathcal P$ be its stackification [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] for the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site], with pullback-compatible functor $i:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$. Write $\pi:h_U\to\mathcal Q$ for the functor sending $u\in U(T)$ to $i(u)$. Then the diagonal of $\mathcal Q$ is representable by algebraic spaces: every $\operatorname{Isom}_T(a,b)$ for $a,b\in\mathcal Q(T)$ is an algebraic space over $T$. For every scheme $T$ and $q\in\mathcal Q(T)$, the 2-fibre product $h_T\times_{q,\mathcal Q,\pi}h_U$ is represented by an algebraic space smooth and surjective over $T$. Here $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$ is a discrete groupoid; a 2-fibre product has objects consisting of two objects and an isomorphism of their images. The natural map $R\to h_U\times_{\pi,\mathcal Q,\pi}h_U$, sending $r\in R(T)$ to $(s(r),t(r),i(r))$ with $i(r):i(s(r))\to i(t(r))$ the image of the arrow $r$, is an equivalence. In particular $\mathcal Q$ is an algebraic stack: an fppf stack with representable diagonal and smooth surjective scheme atlas.

proof.text: For $u,v\in U(T)$, the arrow presheaf from $u$ to $v$ is $T\times_{(u,v),U\times_SU,(s,t)}R$. It is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], hence an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The Isom clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] therefore says that its map to $\operatorname{Isom}(i(u),i(v))$ is an isomorphism: sheafifying a sheaf fixes it, by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. This proves full faithfulness on these object pairs, naturally under base change. Here and below an algebraic space over $S$ with a map to an $S$-scheme $Z$ is the same as an algebraic space over $Z$: in either direction the sections over a test scheme correspond, a scheme chart stays a representable surjective etale chart, and the scheme fibre products testing the diagonal are the same sheaves, so [def-trf-algebraic-space] is checked directly.

proof.text: On every test scheme $T$, objects of $h_U\times_{\mathcal Q}h_U$ are triples $(u,v,\alpha:i(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}i(v))$. Step 1 gives a unique $r\in R(T)$ with $s(r)=u$, $t(r)=v$ and $i(r)=\alpha$. Since both factors $h_U$ are discrete, a morphism between two triples exists only for equal $u,v,\alpha$, and is then the identity. These bijections commute with pullback, so the specified map from $R$ is an equivalence of fibred groupoids. This is the required kernel-pair assertion.

For $a,b\in\mathcal Q(T)$ choose successive fppf coverings on which both are isomorphic to $i(u_i),i(v_i)$, using [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Their Isom sheaf is locally the algebraic space of step 1. Conjugation by the chosen isomorphisms identifies these sheaves, since $\alpha\mapsto\beta_i\alpha\alpha_i^{-1}$ has inverse $\gamma\mapsto\beta_i^{-1}\gamma\alpha_i$. Refine the covering by keeping, for each point of $T$, one member whose image contains it: it is still an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], the restricted isomorphisms persist, and its index set has at most the cardinality of the point set of $T$. Choose etale scheme charts of the local spaces, objects of the big site. The charts and this index set lie in the working Grothendieck universe [def-weil-size-convention]; their disjoint union is a scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], small in that universe, so it is admitted in the chosen ambient big site. The chart condition also gives an algebraic-space coproduct by [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct]. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-local-algebraic-space] to the Isom sheaf, which is a sheaf because $\mathcal Q$ is a stack. Thus every Isom sheaf is an algebraic space: the asserted representable diagonal.

Fix $q\in\mathcal Q(T)$ and form the scheme $B=T\times_SU$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Over $B$, apply step 3 to the pullbacks of $q$ and the tautological object $\pi(\operatorname{pr}_U)$. Its Isom sheaf is an algebraic space $F/B$. By the remark at the end of step 1 it is also an algebraic space over $S$, with a map to $T$ through $B\to T$; a section over $T'$ is a map $T'\to B$ and a section of $F$ over it. Viewed over $T$, its test objects are precisely $(u,\alpha:q|_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}i(u))$ for $T'\to T$, with only identity morphisms. Hence $F$ represents $h_T\times_{\mathcal Q}h_U$, including its projection to $T$.

proof.text: Choose an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and isomorphisms $q|_{T_i}\cong i(v_i)$ by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Replacing $\alpha:q\to i(u)$ by its composite with $i(v_i)\to q$, steps 1 and 2 identify $F\times_TT_i$ with $R\times_{s,U,v_i}T_i$. The projection is smooth by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality], since $s$ is smooth. It is surjective: $z\mapsto(e(v_i(z)),z)$ is a section, so every field-valued point has a lift with the same field. This checks surjectivity without a finiteness or separatedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 04X0 (lemma-smooth-quotient-smooth-presentation), local calculation and identity section.

proof.text: Apply fppf target locality in [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] to the algebraic-space morphism $F\to T$ from step 4 and its covering in step 5. It is smooth and surjective. This holds for every $T,q$, so $\pi$ is a smooth surjective atlas from the given scheme $U$. Finally [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] supplies the fppf stack condition, step 3 the representable diagonal, and the preceding calculation the atlas. These are exactly the three conditions of an algebraic stack in the statement.
